name: Liepāja
title: Liepāja Ship Thickness Measurement & UTM Services
description: Ship thickness measurement in Liepāja for coasters, fishing vessels and bulk carriers: UTM of hull structure, pre-docking gauging and renewal survey work.
h1: Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging at the Port of Liepāja
intro: Liepāja is an ice-free port on Latvia's south-west coast with grain, timber and general cargo berths, a fishing harbour and the Tosmare ship-repair yard. Many of the ships docking here are smaller and older short-sea vessels whose renewal surveys bring a good deal of steel. Our technicians are mobilised from India to Liepāja to measure hull structure ahead of or during the docking, so that the steel list is known before the yard programme is fixed.
keywords: hull gauging at the port of liepāja

highlights.p: The Tosmare shipyard in Liepāja docks and repairs small and medium-sized ships. Gauging at the start of a docking gives the yard and the surveyor measured figures, so renewal areas are agreed quickly and steel is ordered early.

Coasters, tugs and fishing vessels make up much of the local docking traffic. Their thinner original plating leaves a small absolute corrosion margin, so moderate wastage reaches renewal limits sooner than on larger ships.

Liepāja usually stays free of ice through the winter, so dockings and gauging can be scheduled in the quieter months without waiting for ice to clear, and without the escort delays common further north.

port.h: Port of Liepāja: cargo, fishing and ship repair
p: The Port of Liepāja is managed within the Liepāja Special Economic Zone and stretches along a sheltered harbour behind breakwaters on the open Baltic coast. Its trade is regional and practical: grain and agricultural products from Latvia's farmland, timber and wood products, general and project cargo, and a share of ro-ro traffic. To the north, the Karosta area was built as a naval harbour and is still home to the Latvian Navy, while the southern and central harbour areas serve commercial cargo, the fishing fleet and ship repair.

The port's character is set by smaller ships. Bulk carriers and general cargo vessels calling at the grain and timber berths tend to be short-sea sizes, and the fishing harbour handles trawlers and other fishing vessels that work the Baltic. The Tosmare shipyard docks and repairs vessels from these fleets as well as tugs, workboats and other small and medium-sized ships. Many of these vessels are old by the standards of deep-sea shipping, and their renewal surveys at twenty or twenty-five years bring substantial steel renewal that has to be measured, scoped and agreed with the class or flag surveyor.

The work fits the port's rhythm: cargo loading at the grain and timber berths runs over a day or more, fishing vessels lie alongside between trips, and above all, dockings at Tosmare give a fixed period with the hull out of the water. The ice-free harbour means winter is a working season rather than a pause. What makes inspection demand distinctive in Liepāja is the plating itself. On small ships the original plate is thin, so the absolute margin before renewal is small, and pitting or grooving that would be a nuisance on a large bulk carrier can mean a renewal on a coaster. Readings need close attention to probe choice and calibration on thin material, and the reading pattern must be dense enough to catch local wastage.

Dockings at Tosmare are the centre of gauging work in Liepāja. Tosmare's workforce stages the hull and prepares the tanks, and the gauging team works one step behind them, from the keel plates upwards. On small ships the dock period is short, so the first day's readings matter most: they show the surveyor and the yard where renewal is needed while there is still time to order steel and plan the work. For Liepāja ship repair, a gauging report that arrives on the second day is worth far more than one that arrives on the last.

Alongside the cargo berths, gauging follows the loading programme, with holds measured before loading or after discharge, and ballast tanks opened to the team after the crew has aired and tested them. Fishing vessels between trips can be gauged at the fishing harbour, where fish holds, tanks and hull plating from the inside are accessible while the crew is ashore. Ships at the roads are boarded from a launch the agent arranges when the sea allows, which confines the job to the deck and to tanks the crew has opened up.
list: Tosmare shipyard — docking and repair of small and medium-sized ships; bottom, side shell, tank and deck gauging during the docking
Grain and timber berths — bulk carriers and general cargo ships; hold frame, tank-top and hatch-coaming gauging between loading stages
Fishing harbour — trawlers and fishing vessels; hull plating, fish-hold and tank gauging while alongside between trips
General cargo and ro-ro quays — multipurpose and ro-ro ships; deck, ramp and accessible tank gauging during port calls
Liepāja roads — ships waiting to berth or to enter the yard; the agent books a boat out to the ship for deck and tank work

context.h: Latvian regulation and short-sea market context
p: Latvia belongs to the Paris MoU, and ships off Liepāja are held to the 0.10% fuel-sulphur limit that covers the whole Baltic ECA. Most short-sea and fishing vessels meet that limit on compliant distillate fuel rather than scrubbers, so scrubber piping is a smaller part of the work here than in larger ports. Both EU climate measures for shipping, the emissions trading scheme that reached ships in 2024 and the FuelEU Maritime rules that followed a year later, start at 5000 gross tonnage, which leaves many of the coasters and fishing vessels calling at Liepāja outside both, while the larger bulk carriers and general cargo ships fall inside.

Paris MoU targeting puts older ships into the higher-risk categories, and many of the vessels using Liepāja are in that age bracket, so structural deficiencies found by port state control can lead to detention. For the owner of an older coaster, the gauging record is what stands between a planned renewal at a docking and an unplanned one forced by an inspection. Whether a vessel's surveys are carried out by a classification society or by the flag administration, a complete, structured set of thickness readings is the basis for renewal decisions, for pre-purchase negotiations and for keeping an older ship trading.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Liepāja
jobs.p: Most Liepāja jobs are built around a docking at Tosmare, with cargo-berth and fishing-harbour work in between. Scopes are smaller than on deep-sea ships, but the margins are tighter and the dock periods shorter, so planning and early readings carry more weight. Coaster thickness measurement here is usually the deciding input for the yard's work list and for the owner's decision on how much to renew.
list: Renewal-survey gauging on a short-sea general cargo ship docked at Tosmare, covering bottom plating, side shell, double-bottom tanks and hold frames
Hull plating and fish-hold gauging on a trawler alongside in the fishing harbour, ahead of a docking where renewals need to be planned
Deck and ballast-tank readings on a coaster loading grain, taken ahead of her docking so the owner can compare repair yards with measured steel figures
Magnetic particle crack detection on a tug's towing bitt foundations, towing hook seating and winch seatings during a short docking at Tosmare
Pre-purchase condition gauging of an older coaster at the Liepāja roads for a buyer weighing renewal steel against the purchase terms

logistics: We route the team through Riga International Airport and on to Liepāja by road down the Kurzeme coast. The ship's agent obtains gate passes for the port terminals and a launch for vessels at the roads, and for dockings the yard arranges the team's entry to Tosmare. Our technicians travel from India on a Schengen visa issued through Latvian consular channels; the earlier the docking date is fixed, the easier it is to align the visa with the yard programme and avoid a docking that starts before the team can arrive.
vessels: Coasters and short-sea general cargo ships

faqs.q: Can you gauge small ships with thin plating accurately?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right probe and calibration. On thin plate we use transducers suited to the thickness range and calibrate on a reference block of similar thickness and material. Where coatings are intact, readings are taken through the coating in a mode that excludes it. The reading pattern is denser than on a large ship, because local pitting matters more when the margin is small.

faqs.q: Do fishing vessels need thickness measurement?
faqs.a: When their class or flag survey regime calls for it, typically at renewal surveys and dockings of older vessels, yes. Owners also commission it outside surveys to plan steel work, to support insurance or sale, or after damage. The work is the same in principle as on a cargo ship, but fish holds, insulation and tank layouts need planning with the crew.

faqs.q: Can you work alongside the Tosmare yard's own teams?
faqs.a: Yes. Gauging is one strand of a docking, and we coordinate with the yard's planners and the surveyor so that the yard prepares spaces in the sequence the gauging needs. Readings are shared daily, which lets the yard mark renewal areas and order steel while the docking is still young.

faqs.q: Is winter a good time to dock and gauge in Liepāja?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The harbour normally stays open, there is no icebreaker escort to wait for, and many short-sea and fishing vessels are less busy. The practical limits are cold and daylight: couplant behaviour and exposed work in the dock need planning, and we use low-temperature couplant and schedule outdoor shell work for the lightest part of the day.
